rationale: Brute-force detection evidences the enhanced IAM requirement for strong password policy, secure hashing and MFA on critical systems by catching credential-guessing that MFA/lockout must defeat.

Password-spraying detection evidences the critical-systems MFA-for-all and lockout requirement, targeting the low-and-slow guessing that single-factor accounts on critical systems are most exposed to.

External-remote-services detection directly evidences the critical-systems-specific requirement to block remote access from outside KSA and restrict/monitor it inside, by surfacing inbound remote-service sessions to gate.

RDP-abuse detection evidences the enhanced requirement to restrict and monitor interactive remote access to critical systems and enforce MFA, catching lateral/inbound RDP that the isolation and MFA controls must contain.

SSH-session detection evidences the restrict-and-monitor-remote-access requirement for critical-systems administration, surfacing interactive remote logons that MFA and in-KSA-only policy must govern.

LSASS-dumping detection evidences the enhanced secure-hashing and privileged-credential protection intent by catching theft of the authentication material that MFA and strong-hashing policy exist to protect.
LSA-secrets extraction detection evidences protection of cached service-account and machine credentials central to the managed-service-account and secure-hashing requirement for critical systems.

Default-account detection evidences the critical-systems requirement to remove default/backdoor passwords and to use managed service accounts with no interactive login, surfacing exactly those default credentials.
Account-manipulation detection evidences the managed-service-account and no-interactive-login requirement by surfacing unauthorized privilege/credential changes on critical-systems identities.
Local-account abuse detection evidences that the three-monthly access-rights review catches out-of-band local identities on critical-systems hosts that a periodic entitlement review must reconcile.

Detecting rogue local-account creation evidences the quarterly identity-review intent by surfacing accounts provisioned outside process that the recurring access-rights review is designed to catch and revoke.

Malicious-file-execution detection evidences the enhanced host-protection requirement of application whitelisting plus approved endpoint protection on critical-systems servers, catching unauthorized binaries whitelisting must deny.
Malicious-link detection evidences the approved-endpoint-protection layer of the hardened host-protection set for critical systems, catching the initial user-execution vector.

Ingress-tool-transfer detection evidences application whitelisting and endpoint protection on hardened critical-systems servers by catching delivery of unapproved tooling that whitelisting must block from executing.

Obfuscated-file detection evidences the advanced endpoint-protection and critical-file-integrity requirements of the hardened host-protection set, surfacing evasive artifacts signature AV alone would miss.
Process-injection detection evidences the approved-endpoint-protection requirement for critical-systems servers by catching in-memory evasion that bypasses whitelisting and file-based AV.
Mshta LOLBin detection directly evidences the application-whitelisting requirement for critical systems, catching abuse of a signed interpreter used specifically to defeat allow-listing.
Rundll32 LOLBin detection evidences application whitelisting and hardening on critical systems by surfacing proxied execution through a trusted binary that allow-listing policy must constrain.

Registry-modification detection evidences the six-monthly hardening-baseline and critical-file protection intent by surfacing tampering with the configuration and integrity settings that hardening review must hold.

Detecting binaries masquerading as legitimate names/locations evidences the application-whitelisting intent, since name/path spoofing is the primary means of slipping unapproved code past allow-listing on critical systems.

Scheduled-task detection is only adjacency to the whitelisting/endpoint-hardening core of this control: its CTID anchor is CM/AC-centric configuration monitoring, not anti-malware or allow-listing, so it is nominal evidence and does not by itself reduce the risk 2-3-1 targets.

Exploit-public-facing-application detection evidences the enhanced monthly-remediation cadence for internet-connected critical systems, surfacing exploitation of the exposed vulnerabilities this control must patch fastest.

Exploitation-for-client-execution detection evidences the vulnerability-remediation cadence for client-side components of critical systems, catching exploitation of the unpatched application flaws this control governs.

Privilege-escalation-exploit detection evidences the immediate-remediation-of-critical-vulnerabilities requirement, surfacing exploitation of the high-severity kernel/driver flaws this control mandates fixing under emergency change.

Exploitation-of-remote-services detection evidences the quarterly internal-remediation cadence, surfacing exploitation of unpatched internal service vulnerabilities that trusted assessment and updates must close.

Valid-account detection evidences the enhanced requirement to monitor and analyze user behavior on critical systems around the clock, surfacing anomalous authenticated activity for the 24/7 monitoring function.

Brute-force detection evidences the event-log-and-monitoring requirement to enable and monitor authentication logs on all critical-systems components, feeding the round-the-clock security-event analysis.
Web-protocol C2 detection evidences the requirement to monitor critical-systems security events around the clock, providing the network telemetry the 24/7 monitoring function analyzes for beaconing.

Service-stop detection evidences monitoring of critical-systems security and availability events, surfacing attempts to disable services or logging that the 24/7 monitoring and log-protection requirement must catch.

Scheduled-task detection evidences event-log enablement and monitoring on critical-systems components, feeding privileged-persistence events into the around-the-clock analysis and file/change-integrity alerting this control requires.

Exploit-public-facing-application detection evidences the OWASP-Top-Ten minimum-standard requirement for external critical-systems web apps by catching injection/exploitation of the very weakness classes OWASP hardening addresses.

Web-shell detection evidences the OWASP-aligned web-application security requirement by catching the post-exploitation implant that injection and upload flaws (OWASP A03/A01) enable on external critical-systems web apps.

Web-session-cookie-theft detection directly evidences the secure-session-management requirement (session authenticity, lockout and timeout) for external critical-systems web apps, targeting the session-hijack risk that control names.

Web-shell detection evidences implementation of the defined internal-application cybersecurity requirements (CSCC-only, no ECC equivalent) by catching malicious server components planted in critical-systems internal apps.

Application-exploitation detection evidences that the internal-application security requirements are implemented and effective, surfacing exploitation of the app-layer vulnerabilities those requirements exist to eliminate. (Audit: downgraded to medium — public-facing-exploit technique already high at its true home 2-12-1; not double-counted onto the internal-application control at full strength.)

IIS-component (malicious module) detection evidences implementation of internal-application security requirements by catching backdoored app-server extensions embedded in critical-systems internal applications.

Web-session-cookie-theft detection directly evidences the core internal-application control set's secure-session-management element (authenticity, lockout, timeout), targeting the exact session-hijack risk 2-13-3 enumerates.
